title: What Is the Placebo Effect, Really?
summary: Explore what a placebo is, how expectations and psychological mechanisms drive the placebo response, and why its actual clinical effects remain debated.
evidenceNote: While subjective outcomes like pain relief are well-documented, reviews suggest placebos do not generally affect underlying diseases.

scenes.text: Can a sugar pill make your pain disappear?
A placebo is a treatment with no pharmaceutical effect, like an inert sugar pill or saline injection.
In clinical trials, the placebo response measures any change in the control group after receiving the inactive treatment.
Modern studies find placebos can affect subjective outcomes like pain and nausea, but do not impact the disease itself.
A 2010 Cochrane review concluded that placebo interventions do not have important clinical effects in general.
Placebos highlight the complex ways our expectations and psychological mechanisms influence how we perceive symptoms.
